title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
statement: Heights is an m by n grid. Water flows from a cell to a neighbor of equal or lower height. The Pacific touches the top and left borders. The Atlantic touches the bottom and right borders. Return every cell that can flow to both oceans, sorted by row and then column, as [row, col] pairs.
hints: Flowing downhill from every cell is a search per cell.
Reverse the edges: start at the ocean border and walk uphill, to cells of equal or greater height.
A cell reachable by both uphill searches can reach both oceans.

approaches.name: DFS from each cell
approaches.explanation: Stop at a border of each ocean.

approaches.name: Two reverse floods
approaches.explanation: One flood from Pacific borders, one from Atlantic borders.

editorial: Mark Pacific-reachable cells by DFS from the first row and first column, moving only to neighbors whose height is at least the current height. Do the same for the Atlantic from the last row and last column. The intersection, read in row-major order, is the answer.

examples.explanation: A single cell touches both oceans.
